question: Jif cream cleaner was renamed Cif in the UK.
explainer: Same bottle, same smell, one letter different. Nobody was fooled.

question: Twix first went on sale, in Britain.
explainer: Launched here first, years before America got its hands on one.

question: Bird's launched Angel Delight.
explainer: Butterscotch whip from a packet, and a pudding-time icon was born.

question: Hooch alcoholic lemonade went on sale, kicking off the alcopop boom.
explainer: A grumpy lemon on the bottle, and a moral panic in the papers.

question: Pret A Manger opened its first shop, in Victoria, London.
explainer: Ready-made sandwiches, but posh ones. The lunch hour changed for good.

question: Burger King opened its first UK restaurant, in London's West End.
explainer: Home of the Whopper, three years behind McDonald's.

question: Friends Reunited launched, and everyone looked up their old classmates.
explainer: Peak curiosity about what happened to the kid who sat behind you in maths.

question: Nintendo's Game Boy went on sale in Britain.
explainer: Tetris on the bus, and an endless appetite for AA batteries.

question: The BBC Micro computer went on sale.
explainer: Beige, sturdy, and in every school computer room in the land.

question: Chip and PIN became compulsory for card payments in the UK.
explainer: Introduced on Valentine's Day. No more signing the back of the slip.

question: The Oyster card was introduced on London transport.
explainer: Touch in, touch out. And the eternal mystery of the unexpected penalty fare.

question: The Ford Sierra replaced the Cortina, its jelly-mould shape shocking the nation.
explainer: Too curvy for some. Then everyone wanted an XR4i.

question: BMW launched the new MINI.
explainer: Bigger, German-owned, and somehow still very British.

question: Heineken first claimed to refresh the parts other beers cannot reach.
explainer: A slogan so good it was still being parodied decades later.

question: The Sun declared 'It's The Sun Wot Won It' after a general election.
explainer: John Major won, and the paper was not shy about taking the credit.

question: The Daily Star newspaper was launched.
explainer: Born in Manchester, and never short of a pun.

question: The Guardian switched to the smaller Berliner format.
explainer: Neither broadsheet nor tabloid, and printed in full colour throughout.

question: LBC became Britain's first legal commercial radio station.
explainer: London talk radio, beating Capital Radio on air by a week.

question: "Crossroads", the Midlands motel soap, first aired.
explainer: Famous for wobbly sets, and adored by millions anyway.

question: "Emmerdale Farm" first aired on ITV.
explainer: The farm was later dropped from the title. The plane crash came much later.

question: "University Challenge" first aired, with Bamber Gascoigne.
explainer: 'Your starter for ten.' Still going strong.

question: "Tiswas" first aired on Saturday morning ITV.
explainer: Custard pies, buckets of water, and the Phantom Flan Flinger.

question: "Downton Abbey" first aired.
explainer: Upstairs, downstairs, and the Dowager Countess's very best put-downs.

question: "Gogglebox" first aired on Channel 4.
explainer: Watching people watch telly. And it turned out to be brilliant.

question: "Line of Duty" first aired.
explainer: 'Now we're sucking diesel.' AC-12 and Ted Hastings's catchphrases.

question: "Mamma Mia!", the ABBA film, was released.
explainer: Pierce Brosnan singing. Bravely, it must be said.

question: "Paddington", the film, was released.
explainer: Marmalade sandwiches, a hard stare, and Nicole Kidman as a villain.

question: Brotherhood of Man won Eurovision with "Save Your Kisses for Me".
explainer: That dance routine. Hands on hips, a little point, a little twist.

question: Pink Floyd released "The Dark Side of the Moon".
explainer: A prism on the cover, and the best part of a thousand weeks in the American album charts.

question: Cher's "Believe" went to number one, auto-tune and all.
explainer: Do you believe in life after love? Certainly in life after Sonny.

question: Kylie Minogue's "I Should Be So Lucky" went to number one.
explainer: Charlene from Neighbours, now a pop star, courtesy of Stock Aitken Waterman.

question: Will Young's "Evergreen" became the fastest-selling debut single ever.
explainer: Pop Idol's winner, beating Gareth Gates in the final.

question: Robson & Jerome took "Unchained Melody" to number one.
explainer: Two soldiers from Soldier Soldier. Simon Cowell's first big hit.
